data.text: GSAP (GreenSock Animation Platform) is the industry standard for high-performance JavaScript animations.

data.title: GSAP timeline

data.text: GSAP builds timelines of tweens that you can play, pause, reverse, and scrub. Because it animates the DOM and arbitrary objects imperatively, it handles sequenced, choreographed animation that is awkward to express with component props. React integration uses `useGSAP` and refs.

data.title: A sequenced timeline

data.text: The ScrollTrigger plugin ties animation progress to scroll position, which is how reveal-on-scroll and pinned sections are built. In React, target elements through a scoped ref rather than a global selector so two instances of a component do not animate each other. `useGSAP` cleans up the timeline on unmount.

data.title: Reveal on scroll
Interview angle: imperative animation in a declarative framework
data.text: React re-renders from state; GSAP writes styles directly. The two coexist safely when GSAP only touches elements through a ref and the animation does not depend on React state, and when the timeline is created and disposed by an effect. Mixing them without cleanup is how you get animations running twice in development.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Widely used in professional motion design.
